sources.title: MedlinePlus health topics
sources.description: About 1,000 plain-language health topics (conditions, symptoms, tests, wellness) from the U.S. National Library of Medicine.
sources.attribution: Courtesy of MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine. NLM does not endorse this collection. General health information, not medical advice.

sources.title: Army First Aid (ATP 4-02.11, 2026)
sources.description: U.S. Army manual for non-medical personnel: bleeding control and tourniquets, airway, breathing, shock, head and eye injuries, burns, fractures and splinting, bites and stings, heat and cold injuries, evacuation.
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. Government work); approved for public release, distribution unlimited.
sources.attribution: ATP 4-02.11, Casualty Response, Tactical Combat Casualty Care, and First Aid, Headquarters, Department of the Army, 23 March 2026. Converted to markdown; figures are not included.

params.name: Army First Aid
params.notice: U.S. Army manual written for soldiers; parts of it assume combat conditions (Tactical Combat Casualty Care). Figures are not included. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.

sources.title: Over-the-counter drugs (FDA labels)
sources.description: About 2,300 non-prescription medicines and products (pain relievers, cold and allergy, digestive, skin, eye and oral care, sunscreens, antiseptics) from official U.S. "Drug Facts" labels, one page per active ingredient with the brand names it is sold under. Homeopathic products are excluded.
sources.attribution: U.S. Food and Drug Administration drug labels via openFDA. FDA does not endorse this collection. Not medical advice.

params.notice: Official U.S. label text. Doses and directions differ between products and strengths (for example adult tablets and children's liquids): always follow the label of the product you have. Not medical advice; ask a pharmacist or doctor if unsure.

sources.title: Prescription drugs (FDA labels)
sources.description: About 2,900 prescription medicines from official U.S. prescribing information: uses, dosage, contraindications, boxed warnings, side effects, interactions, pregnancy and children, overdose, and the Medication Guide for patients where there is one. One page per active ingredient with its brand names.
sources.attribution: U.S. Food and Drug Administration drug labels via openFDA. FDA does not endorse this collection. Not medical advice.

params.notice: Official U.S. prescribing information, written for health professionals; very long sections are shortened. Take prescription medicines only as prescribed, and never start, stop or change a dose without asking your doctor or pharmacist. Not medical advice.
